AI chatbots could be restricted for users under 15 in Europe  
Concerns are growing that unrestricted access to AI chatbots may be affecting cognitive development in young users.  

Preliminary discussions among EU regulators suggest potential age-based restrictions on AI chatbot usage, aiming to protect children’s mental development. Early reports indicate fears that overreliance on AI for answers may reduce critical thinking and problem-solving skills in adolescents.  

While no final decision has been made, the proposal highlights broader concerns about how immersive AI technologies impact learning and attention spans. Policymakers emphasize the need for safeguards, similar to existing regulations on social media and screen time.  

More updates expected as the EU reviews digital protections for minors.

🌍 Blocking Iran’s nuclear chief from IAEA conference sets dangerous precedent: AEOI

📌 London, IRNA – The spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI), Behrouz Kamalvandi, has described preventing AEOI chief Mohammad Eslami from attending the IAEA General Conference as a dangerous precedent for all countries, stressing that the agency and its member states must stand up to US bullying and political pressure.

Speaking to reporters at the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) on Monday, Kamalavandi said, “Preventing the head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran from attending the General Conference would set a precedent that would affect everyone. Therefore, we must stand up to such bullying and political pressure.”
​
He added, “This recent malicious action by the US government can only be described as childish behavior.”
​
Kamalvandi stressed that the IAEA and other countries have a duty to pressure the US government to abide by the rules, particularly the agency’s rules of procedure, and to reject pressure on various countries and the international body.
​
The Austrian government, acting contrary to its obligations as the host of international institutions and under pressure from the US, revoked Eslami’s visa, preventing him from attending the IAEA General Conference.
​
The 70th IAEA General Conference opened Monday in Vienna with a broad agenda covering the agency’s annual report, nuclear science and technology, technical cooperation, safeguards implementation, and discussions on prohibiting attacks against nuclear facilities.

Tesla will release a “human” for $20,000

Musk officially confirmed: the first Optimus robots will go on sale in 2027.

And the bet on them is so massive that, to make room for these robots, the company has already discontinued its legendary Model S and Model X cars.

Tesla wants to create a truly universal assistant: clean the house, put things away, bring in groceries, load the washing machine, open the door, use regular tools, and learn new tasks simply by being told what to do.

In short, a new member of the family for every household. And on top of that, a universal worker in any factory.

The target price is around $20–30K, although Tesla has not announced the final price yet.

So Tesla is going almost all-in on this field.
